comments.text: Mini gaming pcs aren’t expensive because they are “cool”. They are a niche product that isn’t widely made for all hardware configurations. It’s not hard to make an average mini gaming pc, and most budget pcs are actually mini pcs in a big case because cheaper motherboards and coolers are often smaller to save costs. Average “real gaming” mini pcs are also not common because the drawback is heat which makes performance worse so when your buying a midrange spec computer with a card like 5060/5070 you really want all the fps you can get. You also worry less about athletics at an average price range. The trouble starts when you get into the high end pcs. For instance most 5080/5090 cards are large tripper fan behemoths sucking tons of power and producing tons of heat, pair that with a oven of a top tier cpu inches from a gpu on full blast and you quite literally have a space heater. This isn’t as much of a problem in a large case because it has more air to circulate and more fans to help it do just that but size it down and it creates quite a bit of thermal limitations. A lot of high end mini pcs are liquid cooled on both the cpu and gpu, not because it’s high end but because there is just no way for regular air coolers to be efficient in that space. You also frequently hit temperature limits with components pinned in the 80c range. This obviously reduces performance which is a sacrifice these pcs make and doesn’t really matter on the high end. Most people that buy these don’t care if their game is running at 140fps or 130 so the performance loss is tolerated. Point I’m trying to make is their price accounts for engineering the damn thing to not burn it self or sacrifice too much performance as well as using high quality components with with custom built elements to make it perform well in such a space. Think of it like server gpus that are dramatically more expensive then the same consumer product partially because of the increased specs like ram but also because they are usually redesigned to be efficient in clusters (many guys side by side on one board) a configuration that would choke and throttle most consumer gpus and that exact R&D is what drives the price up
